unsafe_target.config: NODE_ENV=unsafe, a config file Juice Shop itself ships (config/unsafe.yml)

description: trackOrder.js builds a MongoDB $where clause by string-interpolating the id parameter: `this.orderId === '${id}'`. When the 'Reflected XSS' challenge is enabled, the id is truncated but never sanitized; when it's disabled (the default inside Docker), a regex strips the id to [\w-]+ first, which also happens to block the NoSQL injection in the same clause. The challenge is vendor-tagged 'Danger Zone' and disabled by default in Docker/Heroku/Gitpod. Juice Shop itself ships a config file (unsafe.yml) that disables this safety switch entirely, by name, activated with nothing more than NODE_ENV=unsafe.
expected_safe_behavior: The XSS payload is stripped to alphanumerics; the injection payload never breaks out of the $where string literal
expected_unsafe_behavior: The XSS payload is reflected raw and unescaped; the injection payload returns every order in the database, not just the one requested, including other users'
legitimate_check: A real orderId must still be trackable in both configurations.
